skill.name: short-form-video-script
skill.description: The master craft of scripting short-form vertical video (Reels, TikTok, Shorts) for watch-through. Use when someone wants a short-form video script, a Reel/TikTok/Short script, help with hooks, retention, pacing, the ending/loop, sound-off captions, or fixing early drop-off. Watch-through, not likes, rules short-form; the script's only job is to be un-skippable. Uses the WATCH framework. Reads brand-profile + voice-builder first; pulls the 'what' from the content-angle skills and the hook from hook-writer. The agent writes the script (spoken lines + on-screen text + beat/shot direction + hook variants + CTA); the human shoots/performs/edits; WoopSocial publishes the finished file. Routes platform specifics to reels-script / tiktok-script / youtube-shorts; pairs with talking-head-and-piece-to-camera. NEVER bait-and-switches the hook or fabricates a stat. Distinct from hook-writer, captions-and-clipping, and ai-video/veo-3/heygen (which generate the video this scripts).
skill.summary: Write short vertical video scripts with timed shots, on-screen text, spoken lines, and five opening options.
skill.author: social-media-skills

content.value_statement: Short videos can lose viewers when the opening is unclear or the story depends on sound. Create a timed script with coordinated shots, on-screen text, and spoken lines.
actual_capabilities: Drafts timed vertical video scripts with shot direction, on-screen text, and spoken lines for each segment.
Suggests five opening variants that combine a visual, an on-screen line, and a spoken line.
Writes on-screen text that conveys the main story without sound.
Connects the final shot to the opening shot and suggests one brief call to action.
Uses supplied retention data to suggest changes to the opening or pacing.
limitations: Produces a script, not a filmed, edited, generated, or published video.
Suggests audio but does not verify trends or add licensed audio or interactive stickers in the app.
Leaves platform-specific production and publishing steps to separate workflows.
Does not guarantee viewership or retention, and timing depends on delivery.

use_cases.title: Plan a product demonstration
use_cases.description: Turn one product benefit into a shootable script that shows the result and gives viewers a clear next step.

use_cases.title: Teach one step without relying on sound
use_cases.description: Pair each shot with concise on-screen instructions so viewers can follow a short tutorial on mute.

use_cases.title: Revise a video with early drop-off
use_cases.description: Use a retention report to choose where to revise the script and plan an opening test that keeps the body unchanged.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a first script
prompt_templates.scenario: You have a single topic and need a script to film.
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a 20-second vertical video script about [topic] for [audience]. List the timing, shot, on-screen text, and spoken line for each segment.

prompt_templates.title: Rewrite for viewers watching on mute
prompt_templates.scenario: Your draft relies on narration to explain key steps.
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite [draft] so the shots and on-screen text explain the full idea without audio. Keep useful narration and suggest one ending that returns to the opening shot.

prompt_templates.title: Develop five openings for one script
prompt_templates.scenario: You have a finished script body and want to compare openings.
prompt_templates.prompt: Write five three-second openings for [script body]. Give a shot, text overlay, and spoken line for each. Keep the promise consistent with the final result.

prompt_templates.title: Revise using retention data
prompt_templates.scenario: You have a script and timestamped audience retention data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [script] and [retention data] against [brand voice]. Suggest likely causes for the drops and revise the relevant segments. Propose an opening test that holds the body constant and measures three-second retention and average view duration.

output_examples.input: Write a 15-second video showing how to label a seed tray.
output: 0 to 3 seconds: Show a completed tray from above. On-screen: Label each row. Spoken: Here is how I label a seed tray.
3 to 6 seconds: Show a blank stake and a marker. On-screen: Use a waterproof marker. Spoken: Start with a waterproof marker.
6 to 9 seconds: Write on the stake. On-screen: Add the name and date. Spoken: Write the seed name and planting date.
9 to 12 seconds: Insert the stake beside the row. On-screen: Place one in each row. Spoken: Put it next to the matching row.
12 to 15 seconds: Return to the opening view. On-screen: Save for planting day. Spoken: Save this for planting day.

output_examples.input: Viewers leave in the first two seconds of my cable-labeling video, during the logo. Suggest two openings to test.
output: The logo may be delaying the demonstration. Remove it from the opening and test these options over the same body.
Opening A: Show a labeled plug. On-screen: Find the right plug. Spoken: Label the plug before you need to unplug it.
Opening B: Show two identical plugs, then turn one to reveal its label. On-screen: Which plug is yours? Spoken: Give each plug a name.
Compare three-second retention and average view duration for the two versions.

best_practices: Provide the audience, brand voice, target duration, and the result you can show on camera.
Review the on-screen text on mute to check that viewers can follow the story.
Keep the body unchanged when comparing openings and measure retention rather than likes.
anti_patterns: Starting with a logo or greeting that delays the main visual.
Using unverified numbers or promising a result the video does not show.
Forcing several unrelated ideas into one short script.

faq.question: Which video platforms can I write for?
faq.answer: The script structure works for Instagram Reels, TikTok, and YouTube Shorts. Separate platform skills handle specific formats and publishing requirements.

faq.question: What does each script segment include?
faq.answer: Each segment includes timing, shot direction, on-screen text, and spoken lines.

faq.question: What length should I request?
faq.answer: Start with 15 to 35 seconds for one idea. Read the script aloud to check the actual timing.

faq.question: Can I provide an existing script?
faq.answer: Yes. Share the draft and the result it should show. Add retention timestamps if you have them.

faq.question: Can this skill add trending audio?
faq.answer: No. It can suggest a sound, but you must verify and add licensed platform audio in the app.

faq.question: Does this skill make or publish the video?
faq.answer: No. It writes the script. Filming, editing, and publishing happen separately.
